text:
maria: Heads-up — canary running from last deploy shows p50 regression for short-context prefill traffic. Not huge but consistent: ~+25ms.

aj: where do you see the regression? specific model or hw?

maria: Mostly on A100 pools for the 8k model. Profiling indicates a higher-than-expected fraction of prefill requests are being routed to the decode-optimized kernel path. That path is evicting KV entries aggressively and causing a storm of re-populates. Link to perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.local/dash/abc123 (flame + timeline)

perf-bot: alert: canary_p50_shortctx increased 24.7ms (baseline 42.6ms -> 67.3ms) | kv_cache_miss_rate increased 15.4pp | prefill->decode_routed 26.3%

aj: any recent autotuner changes?

maria: Autotuner sampling on sequence-length histograms changed (PR #1428) — looks like a subtle bias in how we round seq bins for newer cuda archs. The boundary that used to be at 64 tokens is effectively landing around 48 after the change. That causes some short prefills to be classified as long-ish and sent to decode path.

ryan: can you paste the profiler counters?

maria: pasted quick counters:```
prefill_total: 124512
prefill_routed_decode: 32740
decode_kernel_invocations_for_prefill: 32740
kv_evictions_per_min: 1500 -> (baseline 60)
kv_miss_rate: 3.1% -> 18.5%
p50_prefill_latency_ms: 42.6 -> 67.3
throughput_tokens_s: -8%
```

tomas: yikes. That eviction/sec spike explains the latency tail. So root cause: bin rounding + arch-aware kernel picks.

sophia: possible fixes? quick patch or rollback?

maria: I prototyped two mitigations: (A) revert the sampling/rounding change (safe but loses some fine-grain adaptivity) (B) introduce a small architecture-aware bias + hysteresis in bucket thresholds and sticky-bucketing for the first 3 requests of a session to avoid flip-flopping. Option B seems better for long term.

aj: can we test B on canary? config snippet you used?

maria: patch config applied to canary:```json
{
  "autotune": {
    "seq_bins": [0, 48, 128, 512],
    "arch_bias": {"A100": 1.15, "H100": 1.05},
    "sticky_bucket_steps": 3,
    "boundary_hysteresis_tokens": 8
  }
}
```

ryan: curious about numbers after canary.

tomas: ran 10k synthetic mixed requests (70% <64, 30% >64) against the canary pool with the new sticky/hysteresis config:
- prefill_routed_decode dropped from 26.3% -> 3.2%
- kv_miss_rate dropped 18.5% -> 4.1%
- p50_prefill_latency 67.3 -> 39.8 (baseline 42.6)
- throughput tokens/sec +2.4%

perf-bot: canary_deploy started by deploy-bot at 1901234700
deploy-bot: canary deployment succeeded on subset (10%) at 1901234760

sophia: great signal. Are we confident no other workloads will be harmed (long-only workloads)?

maria: tested long-only synthetic (>=256). Slight p50 regression ~+4ms on decode path due to sticky behavior (we bias toward prefill kernels occasionally). But end-to-end throughput unchanged and tail stable. Tradeoff looks acceptable; we can make arch_bias opt-in per customer tier if needed.

aj: add a regression test to CI that runs mixed short/long and asserts kv_miss_rate < 6% and prefill->decode_routed < 5% for A100.

ryan: and add a unit test around the histogram sampling so rounding drift can't silently change boundaries again.

maria: will open PR with both tests + a small telemetry event when bucket boundary changes more than 10 tokens. tagging @eng-sre for monitoring.

perf-bot: ticket created: PERF-3214 (autotuner boundary drift + sticky-bucket mitigation)

tomas: PR landed to canary branch, rolling full rollout after another 2h observation window.

maria: TY everyone. I'll follow up with a short postmortem if anything else shows up. :thumbsup:

ryan: quick follow: add note in release notes about the behavior change (sticky first-3 requests) so customers debugging perf see the change.

sophia: agreed. Also add a dashboard panel for bucket churn rate per pool.

maria: added to PERF-3214 backlog. Closing thread for now unless we see new regressions.
